chapters.category: Ethiopic textual tradition • Modern English research translation
chapters.title: Chapter 38 — The First Parable: Judgment and Revealed Light
chapters.sourceNote: Translated afresh into clear modern English from the earliest complete primary-language witness available for this chapter. No extant Aramaic or Greek wording has been identified for the Parables. The complete Ethiopic (Geʽez) text preserved in Rylands Ethiopic MS 23 is the translation base for all six verses, including the appearing congregation of the righteous, the Righteous One, the light of the Lord of Spirits, judgment upon sinners and the end of the time for seeking mercy. Repeated titles for the righteous, chosen and Lord of Spirits are retained rather than collapsed into one designation. No unattested wording was supplied, and no modern English translation was used as the translation base.

verses.text: The first parable: When the congregation of the righteous appears, sinners will be judged for their sins and driven from the face of the earth.
verses.study: The first parable opens with public reversal. The righteous who were not the dominant assembly now appear as a congregation, while sinners face judgment and removal. The verdict is attached to their sins, presenting judgment as moral accountability rather than arbitrary exclusion.
crossReferences: Psalm 1:5–6 — sinners do not stand in the congregation of the righteous
Psalm 37:9–11 — evildoers are removed while the meek inherit the land
Malachi 3:18 — judgment reveals the difference between righteous and wicked
Matthew 13:40–43 — judgment removes lawlessness and the righteous shine

verses.text: When the Righteous One appears before the eyes of the righteous and chosen, whose works depend upon the Lord of Spirits, light will appear to the righteous and chosen who dwell on the earth. Where then will the sinners' dwelling be, and where the resting place of those who denied the Lord of Spirits? It would have been better for them not to have been born.
verses.study: The Righteous One and the appearing light define the hope of the chosen. Their works depend upon the Lord of Spirits rather than earthly power. The questions expose the loss faced by those who denied Him, and the final lament states the severity of that loss without taking pleasure in it.
crossReferences: Psalm 37:5–6 — the LORD brings righteousness out as light
Isaiah 60:1–3 — divine light appears upon God's people while darkness covers others
Malachi 4:2 — the sun of righteousness rises for those who fear God's name
Matthew 26:24 — 'better not to have been born' expresses severe judgment

verses.text: When the secrets of the righteous are revealed, sinners will be judged, and the ungodly will be driven from the presence of the righteous and chosen.
verses.study: What was hidden about the righteous becomes public. Their secret faithfulness and suffering are no longer concealed beneath the apparent success of sinners. Judgment separates the ungodly from the community whose true condition the Lord reveals.
crossReferences: Ecclesiastes 12:14 — God brings every hidden thing into judgment
Daniel 12:3 — the wise and those who lead others to righteousness shine openly
Luke 12:2–3 — concealed things are revealed
Romans 2:16 — God judges hidden human realities

verses.text: From that time, those who possess the earth will no longer be powerful and exalted. They will not be able to look upon the face of the holy ones, for the light of the Lord of Spirits has appeared upon the face of the holy, righteous and chosen.
verses.study: Possession and status cease to guarantee power. The light belonging to the Lord of Spirits rests upon people formerly disregarded by the exalted. The verse describes a transformed public order in which holiness and divine favor, not ownership, determine glory.
crossReferences: 1 Samuel 2:7–8 — the LORD brings down the exalted and raises the poor
Isaiah 2:11–17 — human pride is humbled when the LORD alone is exalted
Isaiah 60:19–21 — the LORD becomes everlasting light for a righteous people
Luke 1:51–53 — the mighty are brought down and the lowly raised

verses.text: At that time the kings and the mighty will perish and be handed over into the hands of the righteous and holy.
verses.study: Earthly rulers who seemed untouchable lose both power and protection. Their transfer into the hands of the righteous reverses the prior relation of oppressor and oppressed. The parable does not authorize present private vengeance; it describes the outcome of divine judgment.
crossReferences: Psalm 149:5–9 — the faithful participate in the execution of written judgment
Daniel 7:22, 27 — judgment and dominion are given to the holy ones
Luke 22:29–30 — faithful disciples are promised participation in judgment
Revelation 20:4 — authority to judge is given to those seated on thrones

verses.text: From that time onward none of them will be able to seek mercy from the Lord of Spirits, for their life has come to its end.
verses.study: The chapter closes after the time of decision has passed. Mercy is not portrayed as weak or unavailable now; the warning is that earthly life and opportunity reach an end. The verse urges present attention to the Lord of Spirits before judgment fixes the outcome.
crossReferences: Isaiah 55:6–7 — the LORD is to be sought while He may be found
Luke 13:24–28 — a shut door marks the end of opportunity
Hebrews 9:27 — death is followed by judgment
Revelation 22:11–12 — fixed conditions accompany the Judge's coming recompense

explanation.heading: Chapter teaching and context
paragraphs: Chapter 38 opens the first parable with a sequence of appearances: the congregation of the righteous, the Righteous One, hidden truth and the light of the Lord of Spirits. What was concealed in the present order becomes visible in judgment.

The parable repeatedly contrasts earthly status with divine recognition. Those who possess the earth, kings and mighty people lose their power; the holy, righteous and chosen bear revealed light. The reversal is judicial, not merely social, because it answers sin and denial of the Lord of Spirits.

Mercy and judgment are held together by time. The chapter ends when life and the opportunity to seek mercy have reached their limit. Its warning therefore addresses present hearers: the future verdict makes current allegiance and repentance urgent.

Biblical Connections illuminate recurring themes of light, reversal, revealed secrets and the judgment of rulers. They should not erase the chapter's own titles or prematurely identify every figure beyond what this first parable states.

crossReferences: Psalm 1:5–6; 37:5–11 — the congregation of the righteous, revealed light and removal of evil
Isaiah 2:11–17; 60:1–3, 19–21 — humbled power and divine light upon God's people
Daniel 7:22, 27; 12:3 — judgment for the holy ones and their revealed brightness
Luke 1:51–53; 13:24–28 — reversal of the mighty and the end of opportunity
Revelation 20:4; 22:11–12 — granted judgment and fixed outcomes at recompense
